baseline_summary: Assignment baselines derived in seconds-unit cost c_ij = t_free_i + T(pos_i→pickup_j) + τ_load + T(pickup_j→drop_j) + τ_unload + β·W_ij + γ·tardiness: nearest (greedy O(n) per task, myopic), load-balance (queue work + travel), Hungarian (LAP with TU constraint matrix, dual u_i+v_j≤c_ij, O(N^3); scipy is BROKEN in the image so it must be hand-implemented with brute-force oracle tests), and Bertsekas auction (ε-CS bound nε, ε-scaling polynomial). ETA model: trapezoidal profile T=ℓ/v_c+v_c/a for ℓ≥v_c²/a else 2√(ℓ/a), plus rotation |Δθ|/ω_max, with per-edge EMA calibration κ_e; dimensionally checked. Traffic baseline: corridor graph G_c (~100-150 nodes vs 960k grid cells), capacity-1 resources (narrow corridors, junctions; wide corridors as two one-way lanes), continuous-time reservation table with interval-overlap conflict predicate and safety pad δ_s = d_safe + v_max(τ_c+τ_ctrl) + ε_loc = 0.68 m, prioritized SIPP planning (complete under well-formed pocket endpoints). Deadlock baseline: Coffman's 4 conditions, five warehouse deadlock types (head-on, intersection cycle, endpoint blocking, convoy, local-planner standoff), wait-for graph from token/geometric blocking with Tarjan SCC O(n+e) (detection latency ≤ T_b + tick), Banker safety check (greedy O(n²|ρ|) sufficient test), aging-based intersection priority Π_i guaranteeing no starvation.

proposals.name: CTR — Corridor-Token Reservation traffic manager
proposals.idea: Plan in time, execute by order: prioritized SIPP on a corridor graph builds a conflict-free time-window reservation table; from it a per-resource entry-order precedence DAG is derived (sparse ADG construction) and enforced with corridor tokens; a robot's Nav2 goal is extended only to the exit node of its granted prefix (NavigateThroughPoses goal update, SpeedLimit for headway, BackUp for yielding), so per-robot Nav2 stacks are untouched. Slack-aware precedence switch reorders a delayed predecessor and a deadline-critical waiter when the resulting graph stays a DAG. Periodic re-timing recomputes ETAs in topological order for assignment costs and KPIs. Theorems: time-feasible reservations ⇒ DAG; DAG + finite-time traversal + well-formed pocket endpoints ⇒ deadlock-free execution; switch safe iff DAG preserved. Execution-level wait-for-graph cycle detection is a safety net for unmodeled effects.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Hönig et al. 2019 ADG (order-based execution), Berndt et al. 2020 switchable ADG, Kim & Tanchoco 1991 time-window AGV routing, Phillips & Likhachev 2011 SIPP, Dunkel 2024 sparse ADG, Makino & Ito 2024 deadline priorities, Čáp et al. 2015 well-formed completeness; LSMART 2026 for FMS design choices.
proposals.expected_gain: Zero deadlocks and zero collisions among robots in S2/S3 scenarios (vs Nav2-only baseline that deadlocks in narrow corridors), ≥15% throughput gain over Nav2-only and over look-ahead-free zone mutual exclusion, tolerance to 100 ms comm latency with ≤10% throughput loss, deadlock detection ≤2.5 s and resolution success ≥95% on injected deadlocks.
proposals.risks: Nav2 goal preemption may cause DWA to decelerate at each prefix extension (mitigate with K=2 look-ahead grants or FollowPath stitching); manual corridor-graph authoring effort; local-planner symmetric standoffs (type T5) are outside the resource model and rely on geometric wait-for detection; conservative δ_s may cost throughput (sweep in S4).
proposals.realtime_budget: Traffic tick 10 Hz; per tick O(n) state update, O(n²) wait-for, O(nK) token checks, O(|E_P|) DAG check; SIPP on reroute <5 ms on a ≤500-node graph; total central CPU <0.1 core. Response-time chain (assign ≤5 ms, SIPP+grant ≤5 ms, DDS+simulated latency 5–105 ms, agent+BT ≤15 ms, A* first segment + first cmd_vel ≤100 ms) ≈180 ms mean, ≈230 ms worst; speculative pre-planning recommended to trim worst case.

proposals.name: HRA — Hungarian + Regret-swap Auction under deadlines
proposals.idea: Event-triggered batch Hungarian on an n×K_t cost matrix (K_t = max(2n, idle) earliest-deadline tasks) using congestion-aware ETA from CTR re-timing (W_ij) and a tardiness penalty; followed by 2-opt regret swaps Δ = c_ij + c_kl − c_il − c_kj > θ and a reassignment auction for not-yet-picked-up tasks with a switching cost θ_sw to prevent oscillation.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Makino & Ito 2024 (D-TP / D-TPTS deadline-aware token passing with task swaps); Hungarian (Kuhn 1955) and Bertsekas auction (1988) as components; GCBHA (Wang et al. 2025) for time-window auctions.
proposals.expected_gain: Total travel distance ≤0.9× nearest-first; tardy-task ratio reduced ≥30% vs nearest/load-balance in S1 (Poisson arrivals 30/60/120 tasks/h); assignment compute <10 ms.
proposals.risks: Cost-matrix quality depends on ETA accuracy (spec requires ≤15% error); reassignment churn if θ_sw too small; scipy unavailable so Hungarian correctness must be proven by brute-force oracle tests.
proposals.realtime_budget: Hungarian 5×≤50 ≤5 ms in pure Python; regret swap O(n²); executed only on events (task burst, robot idle, slack violation), not per tick.

proposals.name: Congestion-aware edge weights on the corridor graph (optional ablation)
proposals.idea: SIPP edge cost κ_e·T_e·(1 + μ·occ_e) where occ_e is the reserved occupancy fraction of edge e over the next H seconds, steering new routes away from corridors already crowded in the reservation table.
proposals.closest_prior_work: Chen et al. AAAI 2024 traffic-flow optimisation; Zhang et al. IJCAI 2024 guidance graph optimization; Shen et al. 2026 lightweight traffic map for LaCAM*.
proposals.expected_gain: Small for 5 robots; expected ≤5% reduction in intersection waiting time; reported as an ablation row rather than a headline claim.
proposals.risks: May lengthen routes without throughput benefit at low density; adds a tuning parameter μ.
proposals.realtime_budget: O(|E_c|) occupancy recomputation per reroute; negligible.

evaluation_plan: KPIs defined from logs: throughput λ̂ = N_done/T_win [tasks/h] (cumulative + 10-min sliding), mean task time W̄ = mean(t_done − t_assign) [s], utilisation U_i = T_busy/T_total with Little's-law consistency check L = λW, tardiness and on-time rate, total distance, intersection wait, deadlock count and resolution time, conflict-prediction precision/recall vs near-misses (<0.7 m), response time in the spec's [cmd_time, response_time, latency_ms] format, CPU%. Scenarios mapped to spec 4.9/4.10: S1 assignment benchmark (50 static tasks + Poisson λ∈{30,60,120}/h, 5 seeds, 20 min; nearest/load-balance/Hungarian/auction/HRA; targets HRA ≤0.9× nearest distance, compute <10 ms); S2 traffic (head-on corridor 2 robots, 4-way intersection, bottleneck aisle 5 robots, 1-h random; baselines B0 Nav2-only with robots as costmap obstacles and B1 zone mutual exclusion without look-ahead vs CTR; targets 0 collisions, 0 deadlocks, ≥+15% throughput vs B0); S3 injected deadlocks ×20 (R1 yield, R2 reroute, R1→R2; detection ≤2.5 s, success ≥95%, mean resolution ≤20 s); S4 latency sweep τ_c∈{0,50,100} ms with jitter × 3 pad levels (0 collisions at 100 ms, ≤10% throughput loss); S5 4-hour endurance (0 deadlocks, CPU ≤80%, no memory growth); S6 50-sample response time (mean ≤200 ms); A1 ablations (Banker admission off, aging off, switch off, congestion weights on). Statistics: 5 seeds mean±std, Welch t-test α=0.05; all automated as launch_testing integration scenarios (7 of the ≥10 required).
implementation_plan: Language: Python 3.10 in the existing ament_cmake_python package src/amr_fleet (ROS-free algorithm modules + rclpy nodes). Files: amr_fleet/graph/corridor_graph.py (geojson compatible with nav2_route format, corridor compression, resources/pockets), eta.py (trapezoid + rotation + κ_e EMA), assignment/{hungarian,auction,baselines,hra}.py, traffic/{reservation_table,sipp,precedence,tokens,banker}.py, deadlock/{wait_for_graph,detector,resolver}.py, kpi.py, nodes/{fleet_manager_node,traffic_manager_node,robot_agent_node,latency_bridge_node,kpi_node}.py, config/{fleet.yaml,corridor_graph.geojson}, launch/fleet.launch.py, test/test_*.py, docs/algorithms/{assignment,traffic,deadlock}.md (deadlock.md already listed in docs README). Interfaces: existing amr_msgs Task/RobotState/FleetStatus(deadlock_count)/AssignTask.srv; new PassageGrant.msg, TrafficState.msg, DeadlockEvent.msg, ReportPassage.srv. Nav2 (verified in amr-fleet-system:latest, Nav2 1.1.20): per-namespace navigate_through_poses (goal-prefix extension), speed_limit topic (nav2_msgs/SpeedLimit; 0.0 = no limit, so never used to stop), backup action for yielding, IsPathValid; optional nav2_route DynamicEdges (closed/opened/adjust edges) for R2 rerouting. latency_bridge delays fleet↔agent topics by τ~U(20,100) ms; agent↔Nav2 actions stay local. Unit tests (≥70% coverage): Hungarian vs brute force (N≤7, incl. rectangular), auction nε bound, ETA vs numeric integration, interval-overlap boundaries, SIPP toy graphs, time-feasible⇒DAG, Banker rejects classic 2-robot swap, Tarjan cycles, resolver determinism, KPI Little check, latency distribution. Compute: central nodes <0.3 core total; response-time budget ≈180 ms mean / 230 ms worst with 100 ms simulated latency, speculative pre-planning recommended. Environment: scipy.optimize import fails (scipy 1.8.0 apt vs numpy 2.2.6 pip) — no scipy at runtime; networkx only as a test oracle. Timeline: W1 graph/ETA/assignment+S1, W2 reservations/SIPP/precedence/tokens/goal extension+S2, W3 detection/resolution/latency bridge/KPI+S3/S4, W4 S5/S6/ablations/docs/dashboard.
open_questions: Does the team's A*/DWA continue smoothly when NavigateThroughPoses goals are extended (preempted) at each token grant, or should FollowPath stitching be used instead?
Who fixes the scipy/numpy ABI break in the Docker image (pin numpy<2 or pip-install scipy)? Our code does not depend on it, but other packages might.
Corridor graph authoring: manual geojson (~100-150 nodes) vs semi-automatic skeletonisation from the SLAM map?
Tuning of the geometric wait-for threshold d_dl in wide corridors to catch local-planner standoffs (type T5) without false positives.
Trade-off of the conservative safety pad δ_s = 0.68 m (quantify via S4 sweep).
Should ETA use payload-dependent acceleration (25 kg loads) instead of relying on per-edge EMA calibration alone?

arXiv API was rate-limited (HTTP 429 ×4, shared quota across parallel agents); abstracts were verified via arxiv.org/abs pages instead — a later pass could rerun the API queries to catch any papers missed by WebSearch.
